task: r6t1 - layout-layer feasibility: can one offset constant separate the pin number from the net label?
mode: read-only. No document write, no canvas write, no save. The only file written is this JSON.
revision: r2t1 - accounting corrections after r6t4 (commit ee0fe70); decision unchanged

reasons: no single offset constant exists in the repo, so premise (1) of the task fails on the facts
the pin number y is owned by the vendor symbol (hardcoded, orientation-dependent: deltas -4/-5/0/+0.5), so changing it is a symbol rebuild
the only in-repo lever for the flag name is the flag component position, which is the "thirteen edits" case the standing rules already reject
a symbol-level edit would change all 70 pin-number attributes on this page (45 visible) and any other project bound to the same library symbol
verdict.whatWouldWork: if the host ever gains a symbol-level lever, the safe window is a uniform lift of 4.37-6.42 units (below 4.37 the number stays inside the label, above 6.42 it reaches MCU-33's fixed label at 783.88); downward 3.76-5.81 also clears this label but deepens a neighbour overlap, so upward is the usable direction
verdict.doNot: do not edit the library symbol in place, do not rebuild the symbol, do not move 12 flags one by one, do not shrink the font (already no-go at 3.81/2.85)

answers.one: No such shared constant exists. The pin number y comes from the vendor symbol document; the flag name y comes from the flag component position computed in layout.ts. They are not the same lever, so changing one cannot fix both.
answers.two: Not configurable. There is no y-offset parameter: the only in-repo knobs are the flag component position and netLabelFontSize (font size only). The pin number offset is hardcoded in the library symbol.

twoOffset.premiseCorrection: the task states "any non-zero offset separates them" - that is false: the two ink boxes share their top edge (790.30), so a small shift leaves them overlapping

up.meaning: lift the band until its bottom clears the label top; the bound is the fixed MCU-33 label bottom 783.88
up.sideEffect: moves toward MCU-33: at the 4.37 minimum the band sits 0.93 units above MCU-33's wire (785)

down.meaning: push the band below the label bottom; the bound is the next row's label top 800.48
down.sideEffect: moves toward +3V3: at the 3.76 minimum the band bottom is -1.57 units above the +3V3 run (800)

upperBoundChoice.adoptedWhy: the fixed obstacle is MCU-33's blue label (x 229.33-248.48, bottom 783.88), because it does not move when the pin numbers do; 6.42 is the true bound under the "all 70 move" premise
upperBoundChoice.conservativeWhy: 5.82 comes from the black band ending at 784.48, which is the moving pin-number 32, not a fixed obstacle; using it is safe but understates the window by 0.60
upperBoundChoice.rejected: PA11 measures x 252.85-269.33 in the same frame, x-disjoint from the pressed column x 232-244, so it cannot bound the shift even though its ink sits at y 776-778

twoOffset.downCaveat: the "3.76 downward" figure is the minimum for moving THIS number. Under the document's own "one symbol-level offset moves all 70" premise, 3.76 also pushes the neighbour pin-30 band (799.88-804.73) deeper into the fixed row-805 label (800.48-804.24), where it already overlaps; so downward is the smaller number but not a page-level improvement. Adopted value remains 4.37 upward.

answers.three: A symbol-level change would move all 70 pin-number attributes at once (45 visible; one edit, but in the library, and for every project using C23922). The flag route instead moves 12 of the 13 netflag components individually (the "thirteen edits" case), and each move drags its stub and wire with it. The +3V3 bus is a `part`, not a netflag, so it is outside that denominator; GND is a netflag but sits off the pin rows at (400,840).
answers.four: There is no constant to restore, so "put the original constant back" does not apply. What restoring would actually require: (a) if the flag route was used, move the same flags back and save, then cold-read; but reopening a document re-mints the 13 netflag instance ids, so a byte-identical comparison only holds within the same session - across a reopen you can compare geometry and net names, not ids; (b) if the symbol route was used, the only restore is reverting the symbol document itself, which this repo does not own and cannot address from here; a project-local copy may exist but the original museum copy is unreachable. Minimum snapshots to keep before any attempt: (1) the page document source (or a .epro2 project export) covering all 13 netflags plus the 70 pin-number attrs, (2) the C23922 symbol document source as it is today, (3) the cold-read invariant JSON (21 components / 8 part + 13 netflag / 55 wires / 55 name pairs / 2 pages / MAIN uuid b275cd23e45c4271bead56f66d4f98fe) so "nothing else moved" can be shown after the restore. Without all three, a rollback cannot be verified - only asserted.

arithmetic.note: the -0.91498 offset holds for all horizontal pins; the name-to-number delta is NOT a single value (-4 / -5 / 0 / +0.5 appear), so there is no one constant that covers every pin
